# Scala fact counters (.scala; Scala 2 and 3), for a rule with the shared prompt file-body-oop:
# one per line, label TAB pattern (Java regex), counted over the whole file. The [ignore] line runs
# first and reads the file as the Scala lexer does, leftmost region first: it blanks line comments,
# block comments (nested two levels deep; a third level ends the comment early), triple-quoted
# strings ("""...""", interpolated or not), string literals and character literals, so a "def" or
# "class" in a Scaladoc, a string or a commented-out block does not count. A region that is never
# closed runs to the end of the file, a string literal to the end of its line; a symbol literal ('name) is no character literal and stays.
# "type declarations" counts every class, trait, object and enum declared at the start of a line,
# case classes, companions and package objects too; "methods (approx)" every def at the start of a
# line (members, local and extension methods, Scala 3's infix def too); "givens and implicits" a
# given instance or an implicit val, def, object or class, also with modifiers after the implicit
# (implicit final class, implicit override def, implicit lazy val); "type aliases" a type with an = (its
# type parameters nested up to three levels, the right side on the next line too, an opaque type
# with an upper bound), not an abstract type member (type T, type T <: AnyRef). Counts are regex
# heuristics: a declaration after another on the same line is not counted. JvmFactPatternsTest pins every case; ProfileFactPatternsLinearityTest measures that every
# pattern reads linearly.
[ignore] comments and string literals
type declarations
case classes and case objects
traits
methods (approx)
extension methods
givens and implicits
vals and vars at the start of a line (members and locals)
type aliases
imports
